mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT weekly means rose monotonically from -34.4 to -29.1 percent across t-3w to t-0w, showing the mobility-suppression regime is loosening; transit recovery leads discretionary retail footfall with a multi-week lag, so RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -34.4 at t-3w to -29.1 at t-0w, a 5.3 point gain
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week yet the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the last 28-day mean of -25.6 percent.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES (-23.4 to -19.1) and TRANSIT (-34.4 to -29.1) are improving together, so the joint return of commuting and transit ridership produces a multiplicative lift in weekday retail footfall that neither series alone generates, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in each of the last two weekly readings
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC still fails to exceed the prior 28-day mean of -25.6 percent.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has drifted down from 11.1 to 9.4 percent, meaning a growing share of the population is no longer confined at home; each point of residential decline converts into out-of-home discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 10.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 10.9 at t-1w to 9.4 at t-0w, below the 10.0 threshold
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stays below 9.5 for two consecutive weeks while the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC remains at or below -25.6 percent.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT at -29.1 and WORKPLACES at -19.1 remain far below baseline; if transit falls back below -32 the suppression regime is re-binding on movement, which forces retail-and-recreation activity down over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean falls back below -32 percent
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -34.4 at t-3w and is still 29.1 points below baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses back below -32, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is still at or above the prior 28-day mean of -25.6 percent.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rebounded from -23.0 to -15.3 in a single week while TRANSIT climbed to -29.1; the simultaneous rebound in outdoor recreation and station traffic signals genuine resumption of discretionary outings, and retail spending follows both series upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises above -16.0 in the same week TRANSIT rises above -30.0
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -23.0 at t-1w to -15.3 at t-0w while TRANSIT reached -29.1
failure_condition: The joint condition PARKS above -16.0 and TRANSIT above -30.0 holds in two consecutive weeks but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays at or below -25.6 percent.

mechanism_narrative: The mid-September collapse of PARKS to -23.0 at t-1w marks the end of the outdoor season; as park usage falls and weather cools, discretionary activity migrates indoors toward retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped to -23.0 at t-1w before a partial rebound to -15.3 at t-0w, showing autumn volatility
failure_condition: PARKS falls below -20.0 for two consecutive weeks and the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 28-day mean of -25.6 percent.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is the only category near baseline and it slipped from -3.4 to -6.0 to -5.1; as pantry-stocking demand fades, household spend rotates out of groceries into discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean falls below -5.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -3.4 at t-2w to -6.0 at t-1w and -5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM holds below -5.0 for two consecutive weeks with no rise in the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC above -25.6 percent.

evidence_refs: fact:t-0w shows RESIDENTIAL at 9.4, TRANSIT at -29.1 and WORKPLACES at -19.1 simultaneously
